claims: Privy answered the in-policy release swap with a past privy-request-expiry with HTTP 401 twice, in the earlier run and in its one re-run, with the same body (findings.provider_reply.raw_body_sha256). A 401 is an error reply: the runner never reads a signature from it, and neither outcome record holds a signed hash.

In the same packet, under the same policy id and policy hash, the positive control was signed (ALLOW / SIGNED_FIELDS_MATCH), and the re-run record cites it by hash; the earlier record does not cite it.

The expired request is the frozen release swap body with one frozen header, privy-request-expiry, set in the past; a fresh request is the same body with the packet's future expiry (findings.request_difference).
The app refuses an expired request itself before any Privy signing call (findings.app_expiry_checks).

app_expiry_checks.where: PrivySignerClient._stop: wall clock >= request_expiry_ms, checked before the local authorization (line 153) and again immediately before the send (line 183); the request is then unsent and no Privy call is made (an expiry during authorization comes after the local key has signed the payload)
_prepare: now >= intent_expires_at, before the route quote and any signer call

_recheck: now >= intent_expires_at, run at line 504 after SIGN_REQUESTED is saved and before signer.rpc at line 513, for the approve and swap steps (the revoke uses _release_problem); no test isolates this return
_recheck: now >= mandate_expires_at; the unit test reaches it through the recheck after the quote (line 648), the journey test through the one at line 504 before signer.rpc

check_release: now >= valid_until or now >= transaction.request_expires_at refuses the release; the worker's signer factory admits the release (core/provider_ports.py:730, which reaches check_release at operating_release.py:304) before it builds the Privy client at line 734. The test shows the request_expires_at refusal only, not valid_until or that call order

ExecutionService._revalidate (submission-time freshness, called from _begin_submission at line 442, before tick's submit): an intent at or past its validity is denied; the test shows no attempt is created

request_difference.note: privy-authorization-signature signs the headers, so it differs whenever they do

limits: Privy did not say why it refused: the body has no code or type field the capture rule accepts (error_code and error_type are null), so the refusal is not shown to be an expiry refusal. A 401 can also mean an authorization or credential failure; that the same key and credentials signed the positive control is the controller's statement, and the records do not name the key.

The fresh twin of the expired request was never sent, so no reply shows that the same body is signed with a future expiry; that the body is in policy rests on rule R3 and the v3 row raw.allow_swap_zero_value.
The re-run sent the same request and idempotency key, so Privy may have answered with its stored reply; the two replies are then one refusal, not two.
Control 11 is defined at the HOST layer (quote age, input age, intent and mandate expiry). This covers the provider-side signing cutoff only, and as a builder decision.
The app checks are cited by path, line and test at this commit; the proof builder does not run them.
